What the frames show

Average detections / frame—
Average pair distance—center to center · pixels
Detections near another—within chosen distance
Average clusters / frame—groups of at least 2
How metrics work

Each detection center is a candidate fish position. Pair distance is the mean of all detection pairs within a frame, then averaged over frames with at least two detections. “Near another” is the share whose nearest neighbor is within the chosen distance. Connected detections form a cluster; single detections are excluded. Inch estimates use the paper-grid calibration and are approximate. When the detected count is low, the detector checks close to the crop edge, then may split a large joined region. These estimates are marked in the raw export. Reflections can create extras, and fish are not tracked between frames.
